title: Acceptance of embedded odd majority
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $T$ be a nonadaptive tester for functions from $\{-1,1\}^n$ to $\{-1,1\}$ that makes two queries, has a finite seed space, and samples its seed from a probability law. Suppose that $T$ accepts every coordinate dictator with probability $1$. For any odd natural number $d\le n$, it then accepts the function that applies majority to the first $d$ coordinates with probability $1$.
hypotheses_covered: $T$ is a nonadaptive two-query tester from the $n$-dimensional sign cube to the sign set
The tester has a finite seed space and a probability law on its seeds
Every coordinate dictator is accepted with probability $1$
